ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 WHAT IS AN INLINE HOOK \xef\x82\xa7When an inline hook is implemented it will overwrite the first bytes codes of a windows api in order to redirect code flow. \xef\x82\xa7This kind of technique can be used in ring 3 or ring 0 modes. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 CHARACTERISTICS \xef\x82\xa7 Inline hooking is more robust than import address table (IAT) hooks. \xef\x82\xa7 They do not have problems related to dll binding at runtime. \xef\x82\xa7 They can trap any function call, not just system calls. \xef\x82\xa7 No device driver is required. \xef\x82\xa7 They are widely used in many renowned professional applications and well-known rootkits. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 SOME GOOD UTILITIES \xef\x82\xa7 At the Defcon 17 Nick Harbour has presented a good tool named apithief. \xef\x82\xa7 The tool launches a process in a suspended state. \xef\x82\xa7 It then injects a DLL and hook Win32 API functions. \xef\x82\xa7 The tool can then monitor the api behavior. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 SOME BAD UTILITIES \xef\x82\xa7 Well-known and widespread malware take advantage of this kind of technique to hook key api windows components in order to spy and steal sensitive information from the user. \xef\x82\xa7 One of these famous malwares is Zeus, also known as Zbot, PRG, Wsnpoem or Gorhax. ws2_32!WSASend API hooked ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 Implementing an inline hook \xef\x82\xa7 We inject our dll into the process we want to hijack. (Please see Userland Hooking in Windows) \xef\x82\xa7 The first bytes of the target api are saved, these are the bytes that will be overwritten. \xef\x82\xa7 We place a jump, call or push-ret instruction. \xef\x82\xa7 The jump redirects the code flow to our function. \xef\x82\xa7 The hook can later call the original api using the saved bytes of the hooked function. \xef\x82\xa7 The original function will return control to our function and then data can be easily tampered. https://www.htbridge.ch/whitepaper/Userland%20Hooking%20in%20Windows.pdf ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 WHAT ARE WE GOING TO OVERWRITE \xef\x82\xa7 It is very important to determine what and where we are going to overwrite the bytes codes. \xef\x82\xa7 Knowing exactly how much space we have at our disposal is really important, otherwise we can destroy the logic of the api, or write beyond his borders. \xef\x82\xa7 An unconditional jump will require 5 bytes. \xef\x82\xa7 We need to disassemble the beginning of the target api. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 WHERE ARE WE GOING TO OVERWRITE \xef\x82\xa7 The start of a windows api function is usually the same. \xef\x82\xa7 After XP-SP2 Microsoft decided to change the windows api preamble: MOV EDI,EDI PUSH EBP MOV EBP,ESP \xef\x82\xa7 This allow for hot-patching, inserting a new code without the need to reboot the box. \xef\x82\xa7 We can use these five bytes to insert our own set of instructions. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 WHERE ARE WE GOING TO OVERWRITE \xef\x82\xa7 Another reason why we select the start of the function is because the more deeper into the function the hook is located, the more we must be careful with the code. \xef\x82\xa7 If you hook deeper into the function, you can create unwanted issues. \xef\x82\xa7 Things become more complex. \xef\x82\xa7 Keep it simple and stupid. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 AN UNSUCCESSFUL HOOK \xef\x82\xa7 If we try to hook every function in the same way we can modify the logic of the function. \xef\x82\xa7 In the picture below we have inserted an unconditional jump that destroy the logic of the function. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 A SUCCESSFUL HOOK \xef\x82\xa7 In this particular example the prolog of httpsendrequest API has been hooked with a jump to our function. \xef\x82\xa7 We have used the first 5 bytes of the target function to place our jmp instruction. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 INLINE HOOKING PRACTICAL EXAMPLE (1) \xef\x82\xa7 In this practical example our target is a simple chat system using nc.exe, but every program using WS2_32.DLL!Send Api could be used. \xef\x82\xa7 We want to hijack the sent messages from one of two users. \xef\x82\xa7 To accomplish this task we inject our DLL into nc.exe process and we hook the aforementioned api. \xef\x82\xa7 Then we jump into our function and we change the stack parameters, then we adjust our stack to avoid incovenients and finally we jump again to WS2_32.DLL!Send api. \xef\x82\xa7 This hook example can be used to create more complex scenarios. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 INLINE HOOKING PRACTICAL EXAMPLE (2) \xef\x82\xa7 Before hooking the WS2_32.dll!send API we attach with our debugger to the nc.exe process which is already listening on port 9999. We can see the unhook prolog. WS2_32!Send ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 INLINE HOOKING PRACTICAL EXAMPLE (3) \xef\x82\xa7 Server is listening for inbound connections (upper image) and the client connects (lower image). All is working normally and users are discussing without any issues. It has been replaced with a jump to our evil function. WS2_32!Send ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 INLINE HOOKING PRACTICAL EXAMPLE (6) \xef\x82\xa7 Let\xe2\x80\x99s check our function at address 0x6FAC11D0. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 INLINE HOOKING PRACTICAL EXAMPLE (7) \xef\x82\xa7 The behavior of the chat has changed too :] ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 DETECTING INLINE HOOKING (1) \xef\x82\xa7 Detecting inline hooks is pretty simple. \xef\x82\xa7 Rootkits detectors like gmer, or BlackLight from Fsecure do a good job. \xef\x82\xa7 Let\xe2\x80\x99s do an injection test into Internet Explorer 8.0 in Windows 7 and hook wininet!HttpSendRequestW Api. ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 CONCLUSION \xef\x82\xa7 Inline hooks can be very useful when trying to reverse malware. \xef\x82\xa7 Paradoxically nowadays malcode use this technique to change the behavior of the operating system in order to steal personal information. \xef\x82\xa7 By understanding and identifying hooks, thought, you will be able to detect most public rootkits and malwares. \xef\x82\xa7 We hope this document help you understand and master inline hooks. \xef\x82\xa7 Demo video: Inline Hooking in Windows http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=39G3EVllqWI ORIGINAL SWISS ETHICAL HACKING Your texte here \xe2\x80\xa6. \xc2\xa92011 High-Tech Bridge SA \xe2\x80\x93 www.htbridge.ch\xc2 TO BE CONTINUED \xef\x82\xa7 In future documents we will introduce Kernel Hooking.
